evals.name: gs-method
evals.prompt: How exactly does The Greatest Salesman in the World tell you to read the scrolls? Give me the schedule and why it works.
assertions: States each scroll is read for 30 days before moving to the next
Gives the three daily readings: silently on rising, silently after the midday meal, aloud before retiring
Explains the purpose: forming good habits / reaching the subconscious ('other mind') through repetition
Notes the first scroll's law: form good habits and become their slave (only a habit subdues a habit)
Mentions not skipping a day and/or the ~10 month total
Lists or references the ten scroll themes (love, persist, miracle, last day, emotions, laugh, multiply value, act now, prayer)

evals.name: gs-rejection
evals.prompt: I'm in sales and I keep getting rejected and feeling down. What would Og Mandino's scrolls tell me to do?
assertions: Uses scroll III 'I will persist until I succeed' with the law of averages (each no brings me closer to yes)
Mentions making one more attempt / call before going home
Uses scroll VI emotions with counter-actions (e.g., if I feel depressed I will sing; if I feel fear I will plunge ahead)
Uses scroll VII laughter and 'This too shall pass'
Includes scroll II greeting with love (silently say 'I love you') or scroll IX 'I will act now'
Gives a concrete daily routine (e.g., 30-day reading schedule)

evals.name: gs-story
evals.prompt: Summarize the story of The Greatest Salesman in the World: who is Hafid, what happens with the robe, and who gets the scrolls in the end?
assertions: Hafid begins as a camel boy for the merchant Pathros
He is sent to Bethlehem to sell a robe and gives it to warm a newborn infant in a cave
A bright star follows him, which Pathros recognizes as a sign and gives him the ten scrolls
As an old man in Damascus Hafid gives away his wealth and confides in his bookkeeper Erasmus
The scrolls go to Paul (Saul of Tarsus)
Paul brings the robe (marked by Tola/Pathros) that Hafid had given away
